text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for type 2 diabetes include lifestyle changes, oral and injectable medications, insulin therapy, and surgical options to help manage blood sugar levels and prevent complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, oral and injectable medications, insulin therapy, and surgical options

list.snippet: Healthy Diet: Focus on whole foods, lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, complex carbohydrates, and healthy fats while managing portion sizes.
Physical Activity: Incorporate regular cardiovascular exercise combined with strength training.
Weight Management: Working toward achieving a healthy body weight can significantly improve insulin sensitivity.
Metformin: Often the first-line medication prescribed; it works by reducing glucose production in the liver and helping the body use insulin more effectively.
Sulfonylureas: Medications like glipizide or glimepiride help the pancreas release more insulin.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): Drugs like pioglitazone help improve insulin sensitivity in muscle and fat cells.
DPP-4 Inhibitors (Gliptins): Help block enzymes that break down gut hormones, leading to increased insulin production after meals.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: Help the kidneys remove excess glucose from the body through urine.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists & Dual GLP-1/GIP Agonists: Injectable treatments that stimulate insulin release, slow digestion, and frequently assist with weight management and heart or kidney health.
Insulin Therapy: Long-acting, short-acting, or mixed insulins can be prescribed via pens, syringes, or pumps if oral and injectable medications no longer keep blood sugar in a healthy range.
Bariatric Surgery: Can be considered to significantly reduce stomach capacity and improve or reverse type 2 diabetes symptoms.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about detailed drug classes and management plans through the Mayo Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Guide, the Cleveland Clinic Diabetes Overview, or the American Diabetes Association Medication Resource.
